text:
maria: FYI deploying canary release r2026-03-14-8 to eu-west (10% traffic). Watching metrics.

incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty incident PD-83921 triggered (high error-rate) — service: model-serving-eu-west — 5xx spike detected across canary hosts. Link: https://pagerduty.example/PD-83921

pagerduty-bot: PD-83921 auto-assigned to group `sre-oncall` per policy. Paging primary on-call.

sre-oncall: Ack'd PD-83921. I'm jumping in — pulling logs and rolling window metrics.

kevin: I see a lane of elevated kv-cache misses and CPU on the canary nodes. Error trace shows OOM on the runtime when sequence length > 1024. Reproducer attached.

alex: Confirmed: regression introduced in tokenizer preproc change in r2026-03-14-8. It increases input lengths for certain requests (long prompt concatenation).

sam: Customer impact: at least 3 tenant threads returned 502s for ~6m. Tracking list: tenant-a, tenant-b, internal-test1. No PII exposure.

maria: Mitigation options: 1) quick rollback of canary 2) scale canary pool (adds cost) 3) apply input-length guard at gateway (fast patch). Thoughts?

kevin: I can push a temporary nginx filter to drop requests > 900 tokens but prefer rollback; faster and safer.

incident-bot: PD-83921 updated: escalation to Tier 2 (lead SRE) after 4 minutes without remediation.

alex: Rolling back canary now. Command:```bash
kubectl -n serving rollout undo deployment/model-serving-eu-west --to-revision=2026-03-14-7
```Doing this as immediate fallback — will monitor.

ops-bot: Deploy rollback initiated by alex at commit sha abcdef1. Started rolling pods.

maria: Noted we still need to ack customers and mark incident status. Sam — can you prepare a short customer note? Keep it factual.

sam: Draft to customers: "We observed an elevated error rate affecting a subset of requests in eu-west during a canary rollout. We rolled back the canary and restored normal service by 10:29 UTC. Root cause under investigation. No data loss." Will DM for approvals.

pagerduty-bot: PD-83921 acknowledged by sre-oncall and resolved (manual resolution) after rollback. Resolution note: rollback of canary release restored normal 5xx rate.

sre-oncall: Metrics look good — 5xx back to baseline, latency stable. Handing off to alex for root cause and postmortem.

kevin: Saved traces and heap dumps from the canary nodes to bucket gs://redwood-incident-dumps/PD-83921/ — link in incident ticket. Initial analysis points to tokenizer change that alters tokenization boundary handling causing pathological long sequences for some inputs.

maria: Quick retrospective notes in thread: 1) Canary traffic shaping allowed impact but we saw cross-tenant failures — need stricter per-tenant throttles; 2) Runbook missing quick rollback checklist for model-serving (we had to derive commands ad-hoc); 3) Add automated input-length guard in gateway as a safety net.

alex: I'll open follow-ups: - RFC to revert tokenizer change until regression tests cover long-prompt scenarios - runbook PR adding rollback steps and PD routing checks - emergency test harness for length edge cases.

sam: Customer comms sent. No high-severity escalations from customers so far. Monitoring for any reopened alerts.

incident-bot: PD-83921 closed. Post-incident actions created: PIA-412 (runbook), PIA-413 (tokenizer regression tests), PIA-414 (gateway guard).

maria: Thank you all. Tagging @kevin and @alex for the postmortem. Please add timelines and exact commands used to the ticket. :+1:

kevin: Will add heapdump analysis and a short timeline tonight.

alex: Putting draft postmortem in /docs/incidents/PD-83921-draft.md and will link from ticket.

maria: Closing thread — if anything reopens I'll re-alert. Great coordination.
